solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A time to abandon overdone religious ceremony

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: an overdone phrase is hackneyed, worn out by use
T is the abbreviation for time; 'A' says only one of them goes

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a religious service has become stale and should be shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for overdone has two Ts; dropping one of them, the first, leaves RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal ceremonial act in a religious observance, such as baptism.

clue.text: Review top secret revelation's source after decoding

indicators.note: decoding scrambled text rearranges it, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the source of a thing is where it starts, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of revelation

explanation.surface: An intelligence officer looks back over how a classified leak first came out once the code was cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a looking back over past events, so it serves as a noun for a review.

clue.text: Tea leaf from tea in Paris to impress one female

indicators.note: to impress is to press into something, so one piece is pushed inside another

parts.note: thé is the French word for tea
the Roman numeral for one
the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A tea leaf taken from a Parisian cup leaves its mark on a woman, as in reading tea leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang (tea leaf rhymes with the answer), so the opening words are not about drinks at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a tea leaf is a thief, someone who steals.

clue.text: Boss one in recent times restricted in cramped lodging?

indicators.note: restricted means held short, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud
the Roman numeral for one
of late means recently

explanation.surface: A boss is stuck in poky accommodation, perhaps one confined during lockdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room apartment, which the question mark admits is typically cramped.

clue.text: Went over point, reflecting, having introduced poetry

indicators.note: something introduced is brought inside, so one piece goes within another
a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: a dart is a pointed missile, a point
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone revisited an argument, reflecting on it, and brought some poetry into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went over' could mean reviewed, like the reflecting surface suggests, but here it is crossing a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so 'went over' a stretch of ground is the past tense.

clue.text: Nymph in wood unbalanced, lacking warmth for male

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one piece is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: unbalanced in mind means insane
a dry manner is cool and without warmth
the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A wood nymph has gone mad and turned cold towards men.
explanation.walkthrough: In MAD, the M (male) is replaced by DRY, giving DRY + AD.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a dryad is a nymph who lives in trees and woodland.

clue.text: Last letter in newspaper a sheer fabrication?

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the rest

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a group
the last letter of the alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A final letter printed in a paper turns out to be an outright fabrication.
explanation.walkthrough: Z goes inside ORGAN A. 'Sheer fabrication' looks like a downright lie, but it means a see-through material.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, transparent fabric of silk or nylon, a sheer textile.

clue.text: One in Larkin's position, 51, very naughty boy accepting God

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: from Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'He's not the Messiah, he's a very naughty boy'
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A random-sounding list: a poet's job, a number, and a misbehaving boy with God inside him.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet Philip Larkin worked for decades as the university librarian at Hull. The god goes in just after the first letter of the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkin earned his living running Hull University's library, so his post is that of a librarian.

clue.text: Old city queen featured in play

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to toy is to play
R for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A city of antiquity whose queen appears in a drama, as Helen does in plays about Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city of Asia Minor besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Artist using lathe?

parts.note: surface reading: a painter or sculptor at work
setter's reading: a craftsman who shapes wood on a lathe is named for that action, and a great English painter shares the name

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the artist is J. M. W. Turner, the landscape painter, whose surname is also the trade name for a lathe operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker who shapes pieces on a lathe is called by this trade name, also the surname of a famous painter.

clue.text: Posh mariner in hat avoiding lake and river

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside another
avoiding something means keeping clear of it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a trilby is a soft felt hat
L is the map abbreviation for lake
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: An upper-class sailor in a hat keeps clear of a lake and a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake and river' looks like a pair of waters, but the lake is the letter to drop and river alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tributary is a stream or smaller river that flows into a larger one.

clue.text: Clown Launcelot covering two bachelors in slime

indicators.note: something covering another wraps round it, so the outer word encloses the rest

parts.note: goo is sticky slime
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, twice

explanation.surface: A clown called Launcelot is covered in gunk, along with two single men.
explanation.walkthrough: Launcelot Gobbo is the clown in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Launcelot Gobbo is Shylock's comic servant, the clown role in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Crime related to stolen goods receiver

parts.note: of can mean concerning or related to
a fence is someone who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: A crime connected with someone who handles stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law, a crime or misdemeanour.

clue.text: King murdered in dark and gloomy prison

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown, dark and dingy
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A king is killed in a dark, dismal jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is from Macbeth, where Duncan is murdered in his sleep by Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Duncan is the Scottish king murdered by Macbeth in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: An award taken by Scots river along with other things?

parts.note: taken as written
the DSO is the Distinguished Service Order, a British military award
the Forth is the river that flows into the Firth of Forth near Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A prize is carried off by a Scottish river, along with other things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom closing a list, meaning 'et cetera', i.e. plus more of the same kind.

clue.text: 2 of 25 behind with credit given by wine people

parts.note: to be behind a cause is to back it, to be for it
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue whose surface is bare instructions about credit, wine and people.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is THIEF and 25 is TIME: the proverb runs 'Procrastination is the thief of time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb by Edward Young calls delay the thief of time, so the cross-referenced phrase names putting things off.

clue.text: What's observed in 27, flying low, unable to change course?

indicators.note: flying suggests scattered through the air, so these letters are thrown into a new order
to change course is to alter direction, so the letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something seen among the stars, flying low and unable to change direction, like a stricken bird or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the GREAT BEAR, Ursa Major, the constellation where astronomers find this planetary nebula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Owl Nebula, Messier 97, is a planetary nebula in Ursa Major, so astronomers observe it there.

clue.text: Broke in thus — lever initially opening

parts.note: taken as written
so means thus

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of lever
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in this way, with a lever wedged into an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke in' reads as a burglary, but 'Broke' alone is the definition and 'in' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke means having no money, unable to pay debts, which is to be insolvent.

clue.text: Company calls about poor lads maltreated in resort

indicators.note: about means around, so the first part goes round the rest
something maltreated is knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for company
taken as written
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A firm phones about some badly treated boys at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company calls' is a single outer shell split around the scrambled lads, not two separate pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a US city at the foot of Pikes Peak, long known as a health and holiday resort.

clue.text: Unthinking nonsense keeping old boy in charge

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: rot is nonsense
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Mindless rubbish is kept going by a former pupil now in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic behaviour is mechanical and automatic, done without thought like a machine.

clue.text: Deny match official cup ties on a regular basis

parts.note: ref is short for referee

indicators.note: on a regular basis means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A referee rejects the claim that cup matches are fixed regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute is to prove a claim false or to reject it, so it means deny.

clue.text: Skate home? Notice daughter holding a book

indicators.note: holding something means having it within, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: to notice is to see
the standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the skating is and spots their daughter reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The skate is the flat fish, not footwear; SEE + D holds A B.
explanation.definitionFit: The skate is a bottom-dwelling ray, so the sea floor is where it lives.

clue.text: Find good university in Bath

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the last word

parts.note: a dip is a bathe, a quick swim
the standard abbreviation for university
the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone finds a good university in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English spa city with a university, but here it is the common noun for a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig something up is to unearth or discover it, as a journalist finds information.

clue.text: Upheaval at Cape Canaveral?

parts.note: surface reading: turmoil or disruption at the space centre
setter's reading: a literal heaving upward, as a rocket rises from the Florida launch pad

explanation.walkthrough: Upheaval usually means social disorder; read literally it is something heaved up, which at the Florida launch site means a rocket leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the moment a rocket or spacecraft rises from its launch pad, as at the Kennedy Space Center.

clue.text: Is it extra stout that's inside to be selected?

indicators.note: that's inside points to letters sitting within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A question about whether a drinker's extra-strong stout is in line to be picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer, but extra stout here describes a very fat person.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means fat in build, so extra stout is very fat, which is the meaning of obese.

clue.text: Frenchman in relationship for an age?

indicators.note: in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a tie is a bond or relationship
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman stays in a long relationship, perhaps for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Time and age both mean an era or period, as in 'the time of the Tudors'.

clue.text: Short stay in French hotel for White House resident?

parts.note: a short stay is one night
puts the night's stay into French: une nuit, one night, with one as I

explanation.surface: A brief visit to a French hotel is booked for someone living at the presidential residence in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: One night in a French hotel is 'une nuit'; write 'une' as I (one) and NUIT follows. The White House is not the US one but an igloo, a house of white snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Inuit, Arctic peoples of Canada and Greenland, traditionally built igloos of snow, so they live in a white house.

clue.text: Ecstasy taken into pub by super star group

parts.note: great means super, excellent

indicators.note: taken into means brought inside, so the drug goes within the next word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Pills are smuggled into a pub by a superstar band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'super star group' reads as a top band; the definition is just 'star group', a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a northern constellation, a group of stars that includes the Plough.

clue.text: Free issue includes image facing the wrong way

indicators.note: something that includes another has it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to issue is to flow out from a source

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means turned around, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A free edition of a magazine contains a photograph printed back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate someone is to set them free from legal, social or political restraint.

clue.text: Network in muddle, as Connery would have had it?

indicators.text: as Connery would have had it
indicators.note: Sean Connery famously slurred his S sounds into SH, so this is how he would pronounce the word

parts.note: a mess is a muddle; with Connery's slushy S it comes out with a SH ending

explanation.surface: A network in disarray, described in the voice of the actor who played James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery, the Scottish actor, had a famous lisp-like slur that turns S into SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net-like fabric of interlaced strands, a network.
